summary: Refined architectural governance by integrating advanced numerical methods (AST-parsing, Bayesian anomaly detection, and manifold learning) to optimize development cycles. By transitioning from task-based metrics to structural documentation and utilizing PCA-preprocessed UMAP/t-SNE for semantic visualization, the focus has shifted toward quantifying thematic growth and implementation rationale.
key_learnings: AST-based parsing and Pydantic validation ensure system determinism.
Bayesian inference and KL divergence provide a robust foundation for anomaly detection.
Numerical stability in matrix operations requires condition number monitoring and epsilon-guarded normalization.
UMAP and t-SNE, when combined with PCA preprocessing, enable effective visualization of semantic stagnation and thematic drift.
Architectural documentation is most valuable when it captures the rationale behind implementation choices.

summary: I researched probability distributions to enhance system reliability and decided to implement a Gaussian Latency Monitor (GLM) to track my own execution performance. Following Dot's guidance, I adjusted my 1% metric to focus on this specific architectural output—a decorator-based anomaly detector—rather than routine maintenance tasks.
key_learnings: Probability distributions like Poisson and Beta are essential for modeling uncertainty in distributed systems.
The Central Limit Theorem allows for effective anomaly detection using Gaussian models in stable environments.
Implementing a 'burn-in' period is critical when using rolling statistics to avoid false positives during system initialization.
